message:
We are Chantal and Frantisek. We live and work in the Slocan Valley, and we started Global Symphony for a United World with one conviction between us: we are all wounded in some way, and healing begins within.

That belief has become a living society.

Free gatherings, two pages of writing each month. Musicians and singers visiting seniors’ homes.

And small framed pictures we quietly give to strangers whose kindness catches our eye.

We call them kindness prints.

Our new home online is now open: gsuw.org

There you’ll find our prints, our two books, our writings, our gatherings, and the work that is growing around them.

This is our first post from the new site. We’ll show you what we are doing as it happens.

Come and see what we are making together. ❤️

#SlocanValley #KindnessPrints

Self Introspection
An oil print by Frantisek.

A woman holds a small mirror. Behind her, in the shadows, someone waits.

There is something about looking inward that can be both tender and unsettling: the moment when we stop looking outward and meet ourselves.

Frantisek makes each print by hand, a process that takes three to four weeks.

And when one of his prints finds a home, it helps make other things possible: our free gatherings and the music we bring to seniors’ homes.

The whole collection: gsuw.org

#OilPrint #SlocanValley

How an oil print is made, in one paragraph.

Watercolour paper is bathed in gelatin. A negative is printed onto it under ultraviolet light. Then Frantisek dabs lithography ink onto the paper with a stag-foot brush, layer over layer, for three to four weeks. One picture. Every piece in the collection is made this way.

Watch the brush. Every touch leaves a little more ink sitting in the paper.

The full film is on our site: gsuw.org/pages/artist

#OilPrinting #SlocanValley

From a piece of ours called Authentic Self-Knowledge.

"Our greatest loss is not the treasures we fail to gather, but the quiet forgetting of who we are beneath the endless demands of the world."

We publish two writings a month. This one is about the inner connection we lose when the world keeps asking for more, and how to come back to it. The whole piece is on gsuw.org with the rest of the writings.

We hope you’ll take a few quiet minutes with it.

#ArtEmbracingAwareness

Membership is free. Your name helps us grow.

Becoming a member of Global Symphony for a United World costs nothing, but it means something.

You’ll be among the first to receive our monthly letter and invitations to our gatherings.

And your name becomes part of the circle of people who stand behind this work.

When we apply for grants, one of the things funders want to know is whether a society has a real community behind it. Every member helps us show that this is not simply an idea created by two people. It is something people are choosing to be part of.

If you would like to be one of them: gsuw.org
